newsitem.title: ZIMBABWE: CRICKET-ATHERTON AND THORPE IN THE RUNS AT LAST.
newsitem.headline: CRICKET-ATHERTON AND THORPE IN THE RUNS AT LAST.

text.p: England captain Mike Atherton and middle-order batsman Graham Thorpe emerged from run droughts on Thursday to score half-centuries on the third day of the match against Matabeleland.
Atherton (55) and Thorpe (65) were top scorers in England's second innings total of 230 for five declared which set the hosts a formidable 377 to win.
Rain brought a premature close with Matabeleland five without loss.

England, who have had a poor start to the tour, began the day well by quickly wrapping up the Matabeleland first innings for 188. In the fourth over of the day Darren Gough had Henry Olonga snapped up by Atherton to finish with the morale-boosting figures of six for 64 as the touring team took a first innings lead of 146.
They quickly lost first innings century maker Nick Knight, lbw to Olonga for just eight, but Atherton and Alec Stewart steadied the ship with a second wicket stand of 78.
Stewart was caught by Guy Whittall at mid-on off slow left-armer Dash Vaghmaria for a fluent 43 and Atherton fell to exactly the same combination shortly afterwards.
By then, though, he had shownd encouraging signs of a return to form, striking eight boundaries in his 103-ball innings of 55 which doubled his total of runs on tour.

Nasser Hussain also looked good in a punishing 40. He added 75 for the fourth wicket with Thorpe who had just begun to master the bowling when he became the third victim of the Whittall-Vaghmaria partnership.
It was just reward for the toiling spinner, who had had the Surrey left-hander survive a stumping chance when he had scored three. Thorpe's 65 came off 101 balls with a six and eight fours.
Atherton declared as soon as Thorpe was out but his hopes of making some early inroads into the Matabeleland second innings before the close of the penultimate day were dashed by the weather.
